authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Operative - Formal Execution.md, §V (attention = ⟨narrow, broad⟩, the ⟨b,d,ρ⟩ meter, path-with-fringes); Ashby's law of requisite variety; Cowan 2001 for the hold this composes with
note: ★★ Reference-less: the two-attention shape exists in the reference **only by convention** and is undeclared. So the counterweight is not a parity grep but **internal consistency** — three constraints already built here that this row had to stay true to.

★★★_the_STEP_0_constraint_that_replaces_.the_risk: ★★★ The salience family closed rival-importance on **four** surfaces — brightness (MON-7), score (UI-1/UI-7), position (UI-13), exemption (CTL-8). A **scoring** attention is exactly where a fifth could open: an operative that could raise its own narrow score would have a rival notion of *important* sitting beside `d(s,V)`, which is the one thing this codebase has spent four slices making impossible.
★★★_the_STEP_0_constraint_that_replaces_.★★★_the_enforcement: `Score` has **no public constructor and no public fields**. The only way to obtain one is `narrow_scan`, which computes `value` from `Region::distance` — the household's own `d(s,V)` — and nowhere else. An operative cannot mint a score, cannot raise its own, and has **no field anywhere** in which to declare a rival metric. Same mechanism as `VisualSpec` (MON-7) and `Capability` (IMM-7), applied to the fifth surface. ★ The absence is checked too: a sustain whose state cannot be read yields **no score**, not a fabricated zero.
★★★_the_STEP_0_constraint_that_replaces_.★_and_the_stance_is_read_not_declared: ★ A second, smaller version of the same discipline: `Aperture::stance()` classifies narrow-vs-broad **off `⟨b,d,ρ⟩` itself**, so an operative cannot call a broad aperture *narrow* by saying so — there is no field to say it in. Which matters, because *both non-empty* is enforced by comparing stances.
★★★_the_STEP_0_constraint_that_replaces_.the_three_internal_constraints_this_row_: ★ In place of a parity half: **(1)** `d(s,V)` and the four-surface salience family — attention must consume the one urgency, not rival it. **(2)** The `⊕` composition tree — depth's substrate already exists as `MonitorEngine`'s parent relation, the same structure `holarchy::escalate` climbs, so no parallel tree was introduced. **(3)** UI-1's `K ≈ 4` — attention's footprint is what may enter the hold, so the two had to compose rather than compete.

divergence.statement: R2, reference-less. The two-attention shape exists in the reference **as a convention rather than a declaration**: `should_evaluate()` is documented *'ALWAYS cheap: threshold check only, zero LLM calls'* against an expensive `evaluate()` — a genuine cheap-scan / costly-look split, honoured by discipline and 27 grep hits. But there is no aperture, no `⟨b,d,ρ⟩`, no cost function, no reframing type, and nothing structural preventing an operative from having only one of the two.
divergence.★★_the_counterweight_the_SHAPE_is_the_re: ★★ The split this row formalises is not invented here — it is the reference's own working discipline, stated in `operatives/base.py`'s docstring and kept: **cheap scan first, expensive look only if the scan says so**. That is exactly §V's economy, and it is why the reference's operative layer is affordable at all. ★ What is missing there is the **declaration**: the discipline is a comment and a naming convention, so nothing stops a future operative from doing expensive work in `should_evaluate`, and nothing says how *wide* or how *deep* a scan may go. This row makes the shape a type and the width a bounded quantity; it did not discover the shape.

term_by_term.cheap-scan before expensive-look: AT PARITY as a **discipline** — `should_evaluate()` vs `evaluate()`, honoured by convention and documented as such.
term_by_term.★★ both attentions non-empty, structural: **THIS SLICE.** Nothing there prevents a one-attention operative.
term_by_term.★★ narrow and broad as different OUTPUT: **THIS SLICE.** `should_evaluate` returns `bool`; there is no reframing notion at all (`reframe` is grep-0).
term_by_term.★★ the ⟨b, d, ρ⟩ meter and κ·b·d·ρ: **THIS SLICE.** `breadth` is grep-0; no cost function for a scan exists.
term_by_term.★★★ depth over the ⊕ composition tree: **THIS SLICE**, and it reuses the tree `holarchy::escalate` already climbs rather than introducing one.
term_by_term.★★★ path-with-fringes rather than subtre: **THIS SLICE**, and structural — the geometric traversal is not expressible.
term_by_term.narrow's score coming from `d(s,V)`: **THIS SLICE** as an enforcement; `d(s,V)` itself is MON-10's and is consumed, not re-derived.
term_by_term.the B_att budget in real currency: NEITHER SIDE — economy-adjacent, and parked with juul-spending. See the limits.

the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★★★ attention (51 hits in the reference,: ★★★ The sharpest false positive in the whole set by count. **Every one is `needs-attention`** — the Monitor's queue of things awaiting a human (`_get_ingest_attention`, needs-attention helpers, the panel copy). A reviewer grepping `attention` finds fifty-one hits and a healthy-looking subsystem, and **none of it is §V's attention**. It is the *object* of attention, not the faculty.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★★ narrow / broad (42 hits between them,: ★★ All the English adjectives, and all in the same honest voice this codebase writes in: *'a narrow, deliberate escape'*, *'deliberately narrow and focused'*, *'a bad/over-broad candidate'*. Named because the pair looks exactly like the row's own vocabulary.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.resolution (15 hits, none the ρ axis): Path resolution, placeholder resolution, `MergeResolution`. Different word entirely.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★ should_evaluate (27 hits, and it is th: ★ The opposite of a false positive and the counterweight's own evidence: the cheap-scan discipline, documented and honoured. Named so it is not overlooked while the noisier greps are being dismissed.

divergence.the_honest_limits: ★★ **`B_att` IS NOW A BALANCE — the limit this vector used to record is CLOSED** (2026-08-18, see the addendum above). `AttentionBudget` makes it a real spendable quantity: `spent` is the fold of an append-only spend list, `spent + remaining == allocated` holds by construction, an unaffordable attention is **refused** (never clamped — clamping is *unsound* here, and proven so), and a refusal appends nothing. `κ_att` is **governed** (PAWA-11) and the module constant was **deleted**. ★★ **WHAT STAYS TRUE**: `κ_att` is still **declared and uncalibrated** — an attention unit and a compute unit are the same word on two unmeasured scales — and **`B_att` is still not denominated in juul**. Bridging them needs `κ_att` and `κ_c` calibrated *against each other*, which neither is, so an exchange rate today would be a made-up number between two declared ones. Parked with the calibration, and named rather than half-wired. ★ **AND THE ALLOCATION IS THE HOST'S**, per operative, deliberately not governed — see the addendum. · ★★ **THE STANCE BOUNDARY IS A DECLARED HEURISTIC** — `b > d·ρ` separates *many things glanced at* from *few things closely*. It is a modelling choice, not a derivation, and it is named as one rather than presented as falling out of §V; what §V does give is that the two are **regions**, and that is what the code encodes. · ★ **THE PATH DESCENDS INTO THE FIRST CHILD** — one child per level is what makes the walk linear, and *which* child is currently the tree's own order rather than a chosen one. A caller wanting the most-urgent child would need the scores the scan produces, which is a real follow-on and is named rather than silently defaulted into. · ★ **BROAD REPORTS THE FIRST FRAME CHANGE, NOT ALL OF THEM** — one reframing trigger is enough to say *the frame you were scoring in has changed*; enumerating every breach would be a second scoring pass wearing a different name. · ★★ **ATTENTION IS NOW CALLED FROM AN OPERATIVE — this limit is also CLOSED**, by the agent-wiring slice: `Agent` holds `⟨narrow, broad⟩` as a required field and `Agent::act` genuinely runs both scans, with what attention chose becoming what `Π` is triggered with. Corrected here because it was still recorded as open, and a stale limit is worse than a missing one. ★ **WHAT STAYS TRUE**: the scan's footprint still does **not** feed `compose_view`'s candidate pool — that composition is real, named in the original limit, and still unbuilt.

both_attentions_cases.name: ★★★_an_attention_carries_both_and_there_is_no_way_to_declare_one
both_attentions_cases.why: ★★★ *A council of one-attention agents is a council of half-minds.* `Attention` has **two required fields, no `Option`, and no single-attention constructor**, so the half-mind is unrepresentable rather than discouraged. The pair's stances are asserted as a **set** containing both regions, so *both non-empty* is checkable rather than argued.

both_attentions_cases.name: ★★★_a_pair_that_is_one_region_twice_is_refused
both_attentions_cases.why: ★★★ The partition arriving through the back door. Two apertures that both land in `Narrow` would satisfy *two fields* while giving the operative one attention under two names — §V is explicit that both belong to **one mind**, not that a council splits into specialists. Refused with the region named.

both_attentions_cases.name: a_zero_axis_is_not_an_aperture
both_attentions_cases.why: An axis at zero is *look at nothing*, which is not a way of attending. Checked on all three, because a zero depth and a zero breadth fail for the same reason and both would silently make the cost zero — an aperture that costs nothing and sees nothing is the worst kind of free.

both_attentions_cases.name: ★_the_stance_is_read_off_the_axes_not_declared
both_attentions_cases.why: ★ An operative cannot call a broad aperture *narrow* by declaring it so, because there is **no field to declare it in** — `stance()` reads `⟨b,d,ρ⟩`. This is the smaller sibling of the score enforcement, and it matters because *both non-empty* is enforced by comparing stances: if the label were declarable, the refusal above would be trivially evadable.

closed_trade_cases.name: ★★_deep_and_narrow_costs_the_same_as_broad_and_shallow
closed_trade_cases.why: ★★ Iso-cost, as arithmetic: `⟨1,4,3⟩` and `⟨12,1,1⟩` both cost 12. The **product** is what the budget bounds, which is precisely what makes the trade closed — the two shapes are the same spend, so neither is the *cheap* one and choosing between them is a choice about what to see rather than what to afford.

closed_trade_cases.name: raising_an_axis_is_paid_for_by_lowering_another
closed_trade_cases.why: The trade run rather than described: doubling depth alone breaks a budget the aperture was inside, and the same depth becomes affordable again once resolution pays for it. **No free axis** — which is the whole reason the meter is a product and not a sum.

closed_trade_cases.name: an_attention_over_budget_is_refused
closed_trade_cases.why: The bound applies to the **pair**, not to each aperture separately: an operative attends with both, so both are spent. Refused at declaration with the cost and the budget named, rather than at scan time when half the work is already done.

path_not_subtree_cases.name: ★★★_the_scan_is_a_path_with_fringes_and_visits_at_most_b_times_d
path_not_subtree_cases.why: ★★★ The property that makes attention affordable at all. Each level samples up to `b` siblings as **fringes** and descends into exactly **one** — so the walk is linear in `d`. Asserted against `path_visits()`, and checked concretely: three mids sampled at level one, one of them descended into at level two.

path_not_subtree_cases.name: ★★★_the_geometric_traversal_is_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE
path_not_subtree_cases.why: ★★★ Structural rather than advised: there is **no `walk_subtree`**, and `scan` descends into one child per level, so a caller cannot request the fan-out. `subtree_visits()` exists **only to measure the gap** and nothing consumes it — at `b=8, d=6` the subtree is over thirty thousand visits against a path of forty-eight. That is why nobody may ask for it, and why the product form in the cost function describes what the walker does rather than a budget it might exceed.

path_not_subtree_cases.name: a_scan_stops_at_a_nano_sustain_rather_than_pretending_to_go_deeper
path_not_subtree_cases.why: A sustain with no children ends the descent, and `reached_depth` reports how far it actually got rather than the aperture's declared `d`. *Asked for five levels, found one* is a fact worth keeping — a scan that reported its request rather than its result would make the footprint a claim instead of a record.

two_output_types_cases.name: ★★★_narrow_returns_a_Score_and_it_comes_from_d_s_V
two_output_types_cases.why: ★★★ The fifth-surface enforcement. `Score` has no constructor, so every score that exists came from `Region::distance` — the household's own `d(s,V)`. Worst-first ordering is that distance's, not an operative's, and a sustain inside `V` scores exactly `0`. This is attention **consuming** the one urgency rather than opening a rival.
two_output_types_cases.expect: the breached sustain first, the viable one at 0.0

two_output_types_cases.name: ★★_an_operative_cannot_mint_a_score
two_output_types_cases.why: ★★ Compile-time in substance: private fields, no constructor. What is assertable at runtime is the other half of the same honesty — a sustain whose state cannot be read yields **no score at all**, not a fabricated zero. Absent rather than defaulted, the `Fraction::of` and `Skew::Unknown` discipline.
two_output_types_cases.expect: no readable state → empty, not zeros

two_output_types_cases.name: ★★_broad_returns_a_Reframing_not_a_number
two_output_types_cases.why: ★★ The load-bearing distinction. Broad reports **that** the frame moved and **where**, and deliberately offers **no magnitude** — a number here would invite a caller to weigh it against a narrow score, and that collapse is exactly what makes an agent a maximiser inside a frame it cannot notice is wrong (Ashby, and §XIV's Goodhart drift arriving through the attention layer).
two_output_types_cases.expect: FrameChanged { at }, with no score field to compare

two_output_types_cases.name: ★_broad_ignores_what_the_task_was_already_looking_at
two_output_types_cases.why: ★ The point of broad is what narrow is **not** covering. A breach inside the task's own branch is narrow's job and reframing nothing; only something outside it triggers. Without this, broad would fire on everything narrow already saw and the two attentions would collapse into one louder one.
two_output_types_cases.expect: FrameHolds when every breach is inside the task branch

footprint_cases.name: ★_the_scan_footprint_can_be_wide_while_the_hold_stays_four
footprint_cases.why: ★ The reconcile with UI-1, in one sentence: **anything can scan widely and hold four; nothing can hold widely.** Pawa bounds the *scan* — what may be looked at this period — and `K ≈ 4` bounds the *hold*. The footprint is the set attention visited, and it is what may enter the knapsack; the knapsack's own bound is unchanged by how widely the sweep went. Two budgets over two different things, composing rather than competing.
footprint_cases.expect: footprint wider than the hold; DEFAULT_BUDGET still 4

★★★_the_B_att_addendum_2026_08_18.what_this_addendum_closes: OPV-7 recorded two residuals that are now FALSE, and a stale limit is worse than a missing one — so both are corrected here rather than quietly dropped. (1) **`B_att` WAS A NUMBER, NOT A BALANCE.** The cost function and a declaration-time bound were real, but nothing was ever SPENT: a second scan cost exactly what the first did, and an operative could attend without limit. That is the same shape of lie as a `debit(amount)` with no reading behind it, and it is closed the same way — `AttentionBudget` makes `B_att` a real spendable quantity. (2) **NOTHING CALLED ATTENTION FROM AN OPERATIVE.** That was closed earlier, by the agent-wiring slice: `Agent` holds `⟨narrow, broad⟩` and `Agent::act` genuinely runs both scans. It is corrected here because it was still recorded as open.
★★★_the_B_att_addendum_2026_08_18.★★★_the_identity_holds_BY_CONSTRUCTION_n: `spent` is the FOLD of an append-only spend list and `remaining` is `allocated - spent`, so `spent + remaining == allocated` is true BY THE SHAPE OF THE TYPE. There is no stored `spent` field that could drift from the spends that produced it — the same discipline as `state = fold(events)` and `JuulLedger`'s balance, one layer up. It is asserted as an EQUATION over a real sequence of spends and refusals, at every step, not spot-checked at the end.
★★★_the_B_att_addendum_2026_08_18.★★★_REFUSED_NEVER_CLAMPED_and_the_reason: The obvious alternative is to clamp — shrink an axis until the aperture fits. It is rejected, and NOT on taste. `Aperture::stance` classifies by `b > d*rho`, so lowering `rho` or `d` CAN FLIP A NARROW APERTURE TO BROAD — and `Attention::declared` exists to refuse a pair that is ONE REGION TWICE, because declaring the same aperture under two names is the partition of the council arriving through the back door. A clamp could therefore silently produce exactly the attention this module already forbids anyone from declaring. So clamping is UNSOUND HERE, not merely unspecified — and that is proven by a case that flips a real stance, not argued. ★ And the operative is TOLD: an unaffordable turn returns `Reasoning::AttentionUnaffordable` rather than quietly scanning less than it declared. Silently over-served and silently under-served are the same defect wearing different signs.
★★★_the_B_att_addendum_2026_08_18.★★_kappa_att_is_now_GOVERNED_and_the_con: `attention::KAPPA` was a module constant read by `Aperture::cost()`. One row after PAWA-11 deleted `pawa::compute_pawa` and both its constants for exactly this reason, leaving a third in place would have been an inconsistency to explain away. So `KAPPA` was DEMOTED to `Parameters::GENESIS_ATTENTION_KAPPA` and `Aperture::cost()` REMOVED OUTRIGHT in favour of `cost_under(&Parameters)`. NO PATH PRICES AN APERTURE FROM A CONSTANT. ★ The genesis value is `1.0`, exactly the constant it replaced, so every already-declared aperture costs what it always did — the whole pre-existing suite passes unchanged, which is the parity evidence. ★ TWO CONSEQUENT DELETIONS, both the same one-truth move one level down: `Scan.cost: usize` became `Scan.aperture` plus `cost_under`, and `SelfModel`'s `attention_budget: usize` field — which stored the COST and called it the BUDGET, a naming defect that only became visible once a real budget existed — was removed rather than renamed, replaced by the attention itself plus `attention_cost_under`.
★★★_the_B_att_addendum_2026_08_18.★_what_is_governed_and_what_is_deliberat: GOVERNED: `kappa_att`, because it is a coefficient of the cost MODEL and one number is the right number. NOT GOVERNED: the ALLOCATION. How much attention THIS operative gets THIS period is a policy that legitimately differs between operatives, so a single governed scalar would be the wrong shape — the same judgement PAWA-8 made about its `Schedule` type. It is host-supplied per operative, and said so rather than defaulted into a global number nobody chose. ★★ AND A REAL LIMIT OF THE GOVERNED HALF: `ParameterSpec` expresses BOUNDED, not POSITIVE, so a governed `kappa_att` of ZERO makes every scan free and the budget vacuous. Note the asymmetry with `issuance_rate`, where zero is a SAFE policy (create no money) while here it DISABLES AN ENFORCEMENT MECHANISM. What can still be said is that it would be a VISIBLE change — gated, recorded, replayable — rather than a source edit.

b_att_cases.name: the_budget_identity_holds_as_an_equation_over_a_real_sequence
b_att_cases.why: ★★★ `spent + remaining == allocated`, asserted AT EVERY STEP of a real sequence of spends and refusals rather than once at the end — because an identity that only holds at the end is a coincidence. `spent` is the fold of the append-only spend list, so there is no stored total to drift, and `spends().len()` is asserted alongside so a refusal is visibly not an entry.

b_att_cases.name: an_unaffordable_attention_is_refused_and_the_budget_is_byte_identical
b_att_cases.why: ★★ The same honest-refusal shape as `Charge::Insufficient`: `OverBudget` reports both numbers so a caller can say HOW MUCH SHORT, and NOTHING IS APPENDED — the budget is compared byte-for-byte before and after, not just by its remaining figure.

b_att_cases.name: clamping_is_unsound_because_it_can_flip_a_stance
b_att_cases.why: ★★★ THE REASON THE POLICY IS REFUSE, PROVEN RATHER THAN ARGUED. A real declared two-region pair is taken, and the narrow aperture's `rho` is lowered exactly as a clamp would — and its `stance()` FLIPS to Broad. A clamped attention would then be Broad twice, which `Attention::declared` refuses outright as `NotTwoRegions`. So clamping could silently produce the one attention this module forbids anyone from declaring: unsound, not merely unspecified.

b_att_cases.name: there_is_no_spend_amount_so_a_cost_cannot_be_invented
b_att_cases.why: ★★★ Structural, and the same mechanism as `charge(&PawaReading)` and `issue(&PawaReading)` one layer down: `spend` takes an `Attention`, which cannot be constructed except through `Attention::declared` — which already refuses a one-region pair and an unaffordable one. So every spend is backed by a real, well-formed attention, and each recorded spend NAMES the attention it paid for, so WHAT WAS THIS SPENT ON stays answerable.

b_att_cases.name: an_agent_that_cannot_afford_to_look_does_not_look_and_says_so
b_att_cases.why: ★★★ The wiring, not just the type. `Agent::act_within` charges `B_att` BEFORE either scan runs, so an exhausted budget stops the turn with `Reasoning::AttentionUnaffordable` carrying both numbers — a FIFTH honest outcome, distinct from `NothingInView`, because an exhausted budget and an empty household are different facts about a turn. ★ The order is deliberate: the charge comes before broad attention's word, since a turn that could not afford to look has not discovered that the frame holds — it has discovered nothing.

b_att_cases.name: attention_is_charged_once_for_the_pair_not_once_per_aperture
b_att_cases.why: ★★ The two attentions are ONE MIND'S. Billing them separately would let a turn afford narrow, spend it, and then discover it could not afford broad — leaving the operative with exactly the half-mind OPV-7's two-required-fields rule exists to prevent. Asserted as an exact figure: one turn spends `narrow + broad`, and the budget records ONE spend, not two.

b_att_cases.name: an_unbudgeted_agent_is_byte_identical_to_before_this_row
b_att_cases.why: ★★ The delegating-variant compatibility pattern, for the fourth time (`run`/`run_with_effect`/`run_under`, `execute_admitted`/`execute_afforded`, and now `act`/`act_within`). `Agent::act` delegates with `AttentionSpending::Unbudgeted`, so every pre-existing caller and every R1 vector is unchanged — and the refusal branch is asserted UNREACHABLE under `Unbudgeted` rather than assumed, by running an agent whose attention costs more than any budget would allow and confirming it still reasons.

b_att_cases.name: the_governed_kappa_is_what_prices_an_aperture_and_no_constant_remains
b_att_cases.why: ★★★ The one-truth proof, one level up from PAWA-11's. The genesis `kappa_att` prices exactly as the deleted constant did (`1.0`, so `<1,4,3>` still costs 12). Then a REAL gated `governance.set_parameter` doubles it, the parameters are READ BACK OUT OF THE RESULTING STATE, and the same aperture costs twice as much — asserted as an inequality against the genesis pricing, so nothing could be silently shadowing it. And a budget that afforded the attention at genesis kappa REFUSES it at the governed one, which is the coefficient reaching the enforcement rather than just the arithmetic.
